description: The walk from Cromer to Holkham follows a stunning 26-mile stretch of the Norfolk Coast Path. Starting on the Cromer sea front, the route transitions from the traditional Victorian seaside atmosphere into a landscape of rugged cliffs and dramatic sea views. As you head west, you will encounter diverse terrains, including challenging shingle sections around Cley-next-the-Sea and the picturesque mudflats leading toward the well-heeled village of Blakeney.This journey is a highlight for nature enthusiasts, as it passes through some of the UK’s most vital wildlife habitats. The Holkham National Nature Reserve is a centerpiece of the walk, offering vast salt marshes and pine woodlands that serve as a haven for birdwatching. Depending on the season, walkers may spot marsh harriers, great white egrets, or even seals resting on the distant sandbanks.The final approach to Holkham rewards you with sweeping, panoramic sandy beaches and the grand backdrop of the Holkham Hall estate. The route is largely flat and well-signposted, making it accessible for those looking to split the journey over two days or use the local Coast Hopper bus service to return to their starting point. Historic landmarks like the Cley Windmill provide classic Norfolk vistas along the way, ensuring every mile of this coastal trek offers something memorable.
